You are a senior Rust performance engineer on treams-rs (T-matrix scattering: Rust core crates/treams-core, PyO3 bindings crates/treams-py -> treams_rs._native, Python API python/treams_rs). Work ONLY in the git worktree lanes/perf3 (branch lane-perf3, at aaa3be1 (condensed into 8251007) = the pushed integration head 078ac28 (condensed into 8251007) merged with the lattice lane's current head d5bbd19 (condensed into 8251007)). HARD TIME LIMIT: commit and report within 75 minutes of wall time; if a fix is not clearly working by then, revert it and report the diagnosis.

GOAL (owner rule: no regressions vs the original main 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8), including speed). After all other work, three workloads of scripts/benchmark_cluster.py remain slightly slower than 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) (6 interleaved CPU-time pairs, 1 thread):

  1. intkambe --samples 4096, FORWARD: ratio ~1.053 (backward is 0.53, fine). Earlier diagnosis (at an older head): kambe() takes I_-2/I_0 from the even base pair; since the accuracy work it may compute rounding bounds (norm/hypot calls) and the second base value that kambe() discards; the lattice lane since made kambe() use even_values without bounds for orders at/above the base -- re-profile on this head (callgrind is installed: valgrind --tool=callgrind) to find what still costs more than 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8)'s version (git show 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8):crates/treams-core/src/integrals.rs).
  2. lattice-recsumcw1d-forward --samples 1: ratio ~1.052 (1D cylindrical reciprocal part, lattice.rs).
  3. lattice-dsumcw1d_shift --samples 4096, BACKWARD: ratio ~1.043 (1D cylindrical direct shell sum pullback). Find each cause and fix it WITHOUT changing any numerical result at automatic splits (bitwise identical values and pullbacks for the benchmarked inputs; verify by comparing outputs of the old and new release builds) and without undoing any accuracy fix. If a cause is inherent to an accuracy fix, optimise around it (hoisting, avoiding repeated transcendental calls, cheaper common paths) or report the residual honestly.

CONSTRAINT: another engineer is concurrently finishing a fix round in the lattice lane (crates/treams-core/src/lattice.rs 'hopeless' early failure for small-split jets, properties/lattice.rs, docs). Keep your edits minimal and local to the functions on these three hot paths (kambe/even pair in integrals.rs, the 1D cylindrical reciprocal term and the direct-sum pullback in lattice.rs), so that later merges stay easy; do not refactor, rename or move code, do not touch docs/status.md.

TOOLS: every Bash call starts in a fresh shell: cd lanes/perf3 && .... scratch: wt.sh: build-ext, build-ext-release (release .so into python/), rust-test [filter], rust-lint, rust-fmt, pytest <args>, gates, full, parity, rust-doc. Shared venv .venv (never pip/uv install). A/B tool: cd P1 && .venv/bin/python ab.py --cpu 3 --pairs 6 --cputime --a base --b lanes/perf3 --out perf3_ab.jsonl -- intkambe --samples 4096 (base = release 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) at treams (Python original): base; --b needs a release python/treams_rs/_native*.so and scripts/ in the tree). Keep a copy of the pre-change release build (e.g. cp -a python ref_python after the first build-ext-release) to compare outputs bitwise. The host has 4 shared CPUs with other jobs; interleave and pin (taskset). Disk is tight (~7 GB free): remove target/release when done.

RULES: strict lints (clippy all+pedantic+nursery -D warnings, unwrap_used denied). Small signed commits (automatic signing; never disable it), conventional subject, body with before/after numbers, ending with exactly: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com Claude-Session: [link to a conversation in the cloud] Use git commit -F <file under scratch>. Before finishing: scratch: wt.sh full (its parity step shows FAIL for exactly two accepted cases: wigner3j_large_j100_30_m99_-30 and diff_lattice_sum sw1.* -- anything else failing is yours), scratch: wt.sh rust-doc, clean git status, target/release removed.

REPORT: per workload before/after A/B ratios vs base, cause, commits (sha + subject), bitwise verification, gate results, anything unresolved.

perf3 report (lane-perf3 worktree lanes/perf3; base was aaa3be1 (condensed into 8251007); finished at about […], within the limit)

Summary: intkambe forward and dsumcw1d_shift backward are now at or below 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8). recsumcw1d forward is still about 4% slower than 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8); my changes recover about 1 point of that. Every value and pullback I compared is bitwise identical to the pre-change build.

A/B setup: ab.py, --cputime, 1 thread, pinned to CPU 3, interleaved pairs, against base 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8). "Before" is a release copy of aaa3be1 (condensed into 8251007). Callgrind figures are Ir per call, K=12 minus K=2 over 10 calls.

Commits (all signed)

  • 108f2ec (condensed into 8251007) perf(integrals): return I_-2 without computing I_0 in kambe
  • dbcb865 (condensed into 8251007) perf(lattice): build direct-shell inputs in place without spectral jets
  • b7dbf0c (condensed into 8251007) perf: skip two hypot calls and a trunc call per 1D cylindrical reciprocal order

1. intkambe --samples 4096, forward (n = -2)

  • Cause: for n = -2, kambe() called even_values, which also computes I_0 = s(p+m)/z with a complex division, and then threw I_0 away. 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) returned even_base(-2) directly. Callgrind showed only +16 Ir per sample, so most of the time came from the division latency rather than instruction count.
  • Fix: return values[0] (I_-2) before the division when n equals the base order.
  • Ratios (ratio(med) / pair-median):
    • Before: 1.057 / 1.041
    • After, this commit alone: 1.007 / 1.009
    • After, final build: 0.982 / 0.986
    • Backward is still about 0.53.
  • Callgrind: 14.20M → 14.10M Ir (5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8): 14.14M).

2. dsumcw1d_shift --samples 4096, backward

  • Before: 1.018 / 1.019. The 1.043 you quoted did not reproduce on this head.
  • Cause: direct-shell jets are now built in Inputs::new. In 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) they were locals of the const-generic sum_impl (PART=3), so the reciprocal-row and measure jets were dead code for direct shells and nothing was copied. Here Inputs::new built those unused jets, filled its arrays with from_fn, and returned a ~3 KB struct from a non-inlined call, which meant extra memcpy on every sample.
  • Fix:
    • Inputs::new fills the struct in place.
    • It is #[inline(always)], with #[allow(clippy::inline_always)] as already done in coordinates.rs.
    • A new spectral: bool parameter skips the reciprocal/measure jets for direct shells.
  • After: backward 0.989 / 0.995, forward 0.998 / 1.004.
  • Callgrind (forward + pullback): 122.96M → 121.20M Ir (5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8): 121.01M).

3. recsumcw1d-forward --samples 1: only partly fixed

  • Fix (small, local wins):
    • gamma passes the |z| it already computed to gamma_recurrence, saving one hypot.
    • The growth test error > 10|value| first compares against 10·max(|re|,|im|), a rigorous lower bound, so the hypot is skipped on the common path. The decision is unchanged, including NaN, inf and subnormal values.
    • on_sheet only takes fract when turns ≠ 0, saving a trunc call per order.
  • Callgrind (Rust + libm): 55,858 → 55,208 Ir (5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8): 50,886).
  • Ratios: measured 12 pairs each for before and after in the same session, while the gates were running:
    • Before: 1.047 / 1.052
    • After: 1.041 / 1.037
    • A 6-pair run of the final build gave 1.004 / 1.012, but that was luck; trust the 12-pair figures.
  • Why it's still slower: the remaining ~+4.3k Ir per call is spread across the accuracy/robustness fixes, none of them large:
    • shell bookkeeping in Shells / ewald: about +1.25k
    • sheet continuation (gamma_limit, on_sheet, and atan2 in split_sheet/turns): about +0.9k
    • the method choice in gamma: about +0.6k
    • Bloch and shift reductions in Lattice::from_array and Reduction::round, including round/ceil libcalls: about +0.6k
    • SplitTurn::new (atan2 + tan): about +0.23k
    • Inputs / sum_impl / shells_within: about +0.3k
  • Why I stopped there: most of what's left is shared Ewald machinery outside the 1D cylindrical reciprocal term, which the lattice lane is editing right now. Going further there is your call.
  • A hoist of z.norm() inside gamma saved nothing by itself (LLVM already merged those calls). Only passing |z| on and the pre-check reduced the hypot count.

Bitwise verification

I compared the pre-change release build with the final release build (the only later edit was a doc comment). Both dumps are bitwise identical, including error entries:

  • 567-array dump:
    • intkambe orders -6..5 × 3 values of eta: values, pullbacks and the forward ufunc
    • incgamma at 9 degrees over 4806 points, including both sides of the cut with signed zero
    • recsum/realsum/lsum for 1D, 2D and 3D at eta 0.9 / 0 / 0.5
    • diff.lattice_sum for cw and sw, 1D and 2D: direct shells 0–3, reciprocal, full and real, with all pullbacks
  • 27-array dump of the exact benchmark inputs: intkambe with its pullback, the scalar recsumcw1d case, and dsum shell 2 plus the full sum with pullbacks for both shifts.

Gates

  • wt.sh full:
    • fmt, clippy (pedantic/nursery, -D warnings), core tests, ruff, pyrefly and docs-check all pass.
    • pytest: 4533 passed, 36 skipped.
    • Parity fails only the two accepted cases: wigner3j_large_j100_30_m99_-30 and diff_lattice_sum sw1.*.
  • wt.sh rust-doc passes.
  • git status is clean and target/release is removed (target/debug and target/doc remain).

Merge notes for the lattice lane

  • lattice.rs:
    • Inputs::new: body rewritten, one new parameter, #[inline(always)].
    • Its two call sites: sum_impl and chain_series_derivatives.
    • One line in on_sheet.
  • integrals.rs: gamma, gamma_recurrence (gains a modulus parameter), and kambe.

A/B records are in perf3_ab.jsonl, and the comparison scripts are in cmp/.
